newsitem.title: FRANCE: Crop observation tool on next Spot satellite.
newsitem.headline: Crop observation tool on next Spot satellite.

text.p: France's Aerospatiale has delivered to the French Space Agency (CNES) the Vegetation crop forecasting instrument to be used aboard Europe's next observation satellite SPOT-4, the company said on Tuesday.
"The main mission...is to ensure the operational surveillance of the evolution of vegetation on a world-wide scale for the prediction of agricultural yields," Aerospatiale said in a statement.

"The European Union will use Vegetation data to support its policies for agriculture, environment, research and international cooperation. The system will permit global observation with almost daily renewal of imagery," it said.
Aerospatiale said Vegetation was 50 percent co-financed by the Commission of the European Union. CNES is the prime contractor for the SPOT-4 satellite.
Slated for launch from French Guiana aboard an Ariane rocket in the first quarter of 1998, SPOT-4 will replace the SPOT-3 satellite that stopped functioning on November 14 after three years in orbit.

CNES said SPOT-3's failure was due to a loss of attitude control and attempts to reestablish contact with the satellite have failed. An inquiry board has been set up to determine the cause of the failure.

The Spot Image Company that markets SPOT satellite data said an earlier generation satellite, SPOT-2, was still operational and efforts will be made to reactivate the first SPOT-1 satellite to avoid disruption of the company's services.

SPOT satellites are placed in heliosynchronous orbits -- circling the earth at an altitude of 822 km (510 miles). Industry analysts said the value of a SPOT-class satellites cost was in excess of $250 million.
